test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 27 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following could be a description of the term 'Financial Inclusion'?

options.text: Delivery of financial services at affordable cost to the poor
Use of mobile phone for financial transactions
Facility of transfer of money free of cost

solution:
The correct answer is __**Delivery of financial services at affordable cost to the poor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Financial Inclusion** aims to provide affordable financial services to disadvantaged and low-income segments of society.
 
• It involves ensuring access to useful and affordable financial products and services such as transactions, payments, savings, credit, and insurance.
 
• These services should be delivered in a responsible and sustainable way to meet the needs of individuals and businesses.
 
• The ultimate goal of financial inclusion is to improve the overall economic stability and empowerment of the underprivileged sections of society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Financial Services:**

 
 
• These include banking, credit, insurance, and investment services that allow individuals to manage their finances and mitigate financial risks.
 
• Examples include savings accounts, loans, insurance policies, and retirement plans.
 
 
 
• **Affordable Cost:**
 
 
• Financial inclusion aims to reduce the cost barriers that prevent low-income individuals from accessing essential financial services.
 
• Affordable cost means low or no fees for services such as account maintenance, transactions, and loans.
 
 
 
• **Know Your Customer (KYC) Norm:**
 
 
• KYC is a regulatory process where banks and financial institutions verify the identity, suitability, and risks involved with maintaining a business relationship.
 
• It helps prevent money laundering, fraud, and illicit activities.
 
 
 
• **Mobile Banking:**
 
 
• Mobile banking refers to the use of a mobile device to carry out financial transactions, including checking account balances, transferring funds, and paying bills.
 
• It is a key tool for financial inclusion, especially in regions where traditional banking infrastructure is lacking.
 
 
 
• **Money Transfer Services:**
 
 
• These services facilitate the transfer of money from one individual to another, often across different geographical locations.
 
• They are crucial for remittances, which are a significant source of income for many households in developing countries.
